LOVETHEOCEAN

The Ultimate Cornwall Day Out

Reconnect with your breath, your body, and the ocean while exploring one of Cornwall's most spectacular coastlines.

Meet your guide and experience the wild beauty of West Cornwall through a unique combination of cold-water immersion, coastal walking, and sea-cliff climbing. Set along Cornwall's breathtaking Atlantic coastline, every adventure is shaped by the tides, weather, and sea conditions, making each experience unique.

Enjoy a refreshing dip in a magical hidden ocean pool while learning simple breathing and relaxation techniques to help you stay calm, work with the cold, and reconnect with nature. Follow spectacular sections of the South West Coast Path, taking in dramatic granite cliffs, hidden coves, turquoise waters, and panoramic Atlantic views while discovering Cornwall's rich wildlife, geology, and mining heritage.

Complete your adventure by climbing one of Cornwall's iconic golden granite sea cliffs. Whether you're climbing for the first time or looking to build confidence outdoors, Annie provides expert instruction, coaching, and guidance throughout the experience.

Designed to reconnect you with nature, build confidence, and inspire adventure, this unique experience combines movement, breathing, and the restorative power of the Atlantic Ocean.

Your Day

Every experience is shaped by the tides and conditions, so no two days are identical. This is a guide to how a typical day flows.

👋

Meet Your Guide (10 min)

Introduction, safety briefing, equipment, and overview of the day's adventure.

🚶

Walk to the Hidden Ocean Pool (20 min)

Follow a beautiful valley trail to a secluded natural ocean pool, enjoying spectacular coastal scenery, wildlife, and Cornwall's rich natural and mining heritage along the way.

🌊

Ocean Dip (60–90 min)

Experience cold-water immersion in a secluded ocean pool or the sea while learning breathing techniques.

☕

Coastal Break (20 min)

Relax, enjoy your packed lunch, rehydrate, and take in the stunning Atlantic scenery.

🏔️

South West Coast Path Walk (40 min)

Walk a stunning section of the world-famous South West Coast Path, taking in breathtaking views of rugged granite cliffs, hidden coves, and the turquoise Atlantic Ocean.

🧗

Climb Cornwall's Iconic Granite Sea Cliffs (2–2.5 hrs)

Experience climbing on Cornwall's iconic, golden granite sea cliffs with expert instruction and coaching.

🐄

Return Walk (30 min)

Finish with a scenic walk back to the meeting point, passing Dartmoor ponies and Belted Galloway cattle grazing the coastal headland while enjoying one last look across the Atlantic Ocean.

The History Beneath Your Feet

This is one of the most archaeologically rich landscapes in Britain. As you walk the Bosigran circular route, you're moving through thousands of years of human history — Iron Age cliff forts, ancient field systems, mysterious underground chambers, and the dramatic remains of Cornwall's tin mining era all lie within a short distance of each other.

Iron Age

Bosigran Castle

Bosigran Castle is a simple Iron Age cliff castle positioned above Bosigran Cliff and Commando Ridge, Cornwall's most iconic sea-cliff climbing.

Iron Age / Early Medieval

Porthmeor Fogou

A fogou (from the Cornish word for cave) is an underground stone-lined passage, the purpose of which remains mysterious — storage, refuge, ritual. The Porthmeor fogou sits within an Iron Age settlement surrounded by some of the finest ancient field boundaries in Cornwall. The settlement itself is believed to have been abandoned in the 5th or 6th century, yet the same massive moorstone boundary walls still stand today — and the farms that surround it are likely medieval in origin.

Victorian Mining Era

The Engine Houses

The two iconic engine houses at Carn Galva were built during the 1850s — one for winding, one for pumping water from the mine workings — and closed in 1875. Restored by the National Trust in the 1980s, they form part of the Cornish Mining World Heritage Site.

Ancient Landscape

Celtic Fields & Ancient Boundaries

The prehistoric field systems around Bosigran and Porthmeor are among the best-preserved in Britain — ancient boundaries still dividing the same clifftop fields they enclosed thousands of years ago. Porthmeor itself takes its name from the Cornish Porth Meur, meaning "large cove." The hamlet lies within the Cornwall Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, a landscape so significant it carries the same protected status as a National Park.

Also look out for the hardy Belted Galloway cattle grazing the cliff tops — their presence helps maintain the coastal grassland, and in spring their work floods the headland with wildflowers. High above, kestrels hover effortlessly over the cliff edge, searching for small mammals in the ancient turf below.
